findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:52-77 — The cancel loop is wrapped in a single try/catch: the first failed SendGrid request aborts the loop, so all remaining reminders are neither cancelled at SendGrid nor deleted from the DB (the collected PrismaPromises are lazy and never awaited on abort). Since the query has no lower bound on scheduledDate, already-sent/past-due batches are included every run, and one persistently failing row re-triggers the abort on every cron invocation, permanently blocking cancellation of all other cancelled reminders.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:214-231 (used from handleCancelBooking.ts:487) — The default cancellation path never calls SendGrid; it only sets cancelled: true and relies on the cron to cancel the batch within 1 hour of scheduledDate. If the cron is down, skipped, or runs less often than hourly, reminder emails are still sent for cancelled bookings — a regression from the previous immediate cancel, and the 1-hour lookahead leaves zero margin even with an exactly-hourly cron.

[Medium/concurrency] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:484-495, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:484-494, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:374-381 and 572-581 — The async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls (which now perform the DB delete/update internally) are fire-and-forget: the previously awaited Promise.all of reminder deletions was removed and nothing awaits the managers. On serverless the handler can respond before the provider cancels or the DB writes complete, and failures are silently swallowed.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:962-974 — The try/catch around the forEach cannot catch errors from the unawaited async calls (they're swallowed inside the managers), so log.error is effectively dead code and the cancellations are unawaited — the error handling is illusory.

[Medium/data] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:215-223 — The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row. In the reschedule path (handleNewBooking.ts:965) the booking row persists, so old email reminder rows are orphaned indefinitely (the cron only cleans cancelled: true rows) and accumulate with each reschedule; the SMS path deletes its rows, so the two methods are inconsistent. These stale rows get re-processed on later cancel/reschedule, producing repeated cancel attempts against already-cancelled batches.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177-186 — twilio.cancelSMS and the DB delete share one try block: if the Twilio call throws, the row is not deleted and no cancelled flag is set, so the reminder remains fully active and the SMS is still sent for a cancelled booking with no retry path (previously the row deletion was independent of the provider call).

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:961-979 — The original booking's reminders are cancelled (immediately at SendGrid for email) before eventManager.reschedule runs; if the reschedule subsequently fails, the still-active original booking is left with its reminders already cancelled.

[Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-50 — remindersToCancel is not filtered by method: EMAIL, scheduled: true, or referenceId: null; any row lacking a valid SendGrid batch id would send batch_id: null and trigger the whole-loop abort described in issue 1.

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:489 vs packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — The two reschedule flows use different email-cancellation semantics (deferred flag vs immediateDelete: true), so the old booking's emails are cancelled with different timing and guarantees depending on which reschedule path executes.

[Low/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:374-381 — The previous deleteMany enforced booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }; the reminder managers now delete by bare id with no ownership check, removing defense-in-depth against deleting other users' reminders if the upstream fetch query is ever broadened.

[Low/api] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder no longer deletes anything in its default path (it flips a flag and depends on a cron run up to an hour before send time); the name and the 'delete' call-site comments no longer match the actual contract, which is misleading for maintainers.

[Low/test_gap] No tests were added for the new cancellation behavior — deleteScheduledEmailReminder's three branches, deleteScheduledSMSReminder's error coupling, the cron cancel loop, and the cancel/reschedule handler changes — despite the significant behavioral shift from immediate row deletion to deferred flag-based cancellation.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:52-77 — The cancel loop is wrapped in a single try/catch: the first failed SendGrid request aborts the loop, so all remaining reminders are neither cancelled at SendGrid nor deleted from the DB (the collected PrismaPromises are lazy and never awaited on abort). Since the query has no lower bound on scheduledDate, already-sent/past-due batches are included every run, and one persistently failing row re-triggers the abort on every cron invocation, permanently blocking cancellation of all other cancelled reminders.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation logic wraps the entire cancellation loop in a single try/catch. Inside the try, each reminder does `await client.request(...)` before queuing the Prisma `delete(...)` promise. If any SendGrid request throws, control jumps to catch and the function skips cancelling the remaining reminders and also skips awaiting/deleting any already-queued DB deletions (the `workflowRemindersToDelete` array is never `Promise.all`’d on error). Additionally, the query filters only `scheduledDate.lte now+1h` with no lower bound, so cancelled reminders with very old `scheduledDate` remain eligible every run, meaning a persistently failing reminder can repeatedly hit the same error path and prevent processing of others.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:214-231 (used from handleCancelBooking.ts:487) — The default cancellation path never calls SendGrid; it only sets cancelled: true and relies on the cron to cancel the batch within 1 hour of scheduledDate. If the cron is down, skipped, or runs less often than hourly, reminder emails are still sent for cancelled bookings — a regression from the previous immediate cancel, and the 1-hour lookahead leaves zero margin even with an exactly-hourly cron.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` so the default path with a non-null `referenceId` does not call SendGrid to cancel; it only marks the DB row `cancelled: true` (emailReminderManager.ts). Call sites like `handleCancelBooking.ts` now invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, so cancellations rely on `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` later finding `cancelled: true` reminders and canceling them via SendGrid only when `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. This creates a verifiable race/regression: if a booking is cancelled less than ~1 hour before the scheduled send (or after the last cron/API run), the reminder may still send because it won’t be cancelled until the next scheduler run, which could be too late; additionally, if the scheduler doesn’t run, SendGrid cancellation never happens.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts` (around the added block under `if (originalRescheduledBooking?.uid)`), the code wraps a `workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a `try/catch`, but calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without `await`. Those managers are `async` (see `emailReminderManager.ts` / `smsReminderManager.ts`), so any rejection would occur asynchronously and will not be caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Additionally, the manager functions themselves catch and `console.log` errors, further preventing the outer `log.error(...)` from ever triggering. The cancellations are also not awaited before proceeding to `eventManager.reschedule(...)`, so the cancellation side effects may race with rescheduling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177-186 — twilio.cancelSMS and the DB delete share one try block: if the Twilio call throws, the row is not deleted and no cancelled flag is set, so the reminder remains fully active and the SMS is still sent for a cancelled booking with no retry path (previously the row deletion was independent of the provider call).

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId) wraps both the provider cancellation (`await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)`) and the DB deletion (`await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`) in the same try/catch. If Twilio throws, execution jumps to catch and the Prisma delete is skipped, leaving the WorkflowReminder row intact. The diff also removed the independent reminder-row deletions at call sites (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts and bookings/workflows routers), so there is no longer a separate DB cleanup path. Unlike the email path which can mark `cancelled: true`, the SMS path has no cancelled flag update fallback, so a failed Twilio cancel can leave an active reminder record and no retry mechanism shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:961-979 — The original booking's reminders are cancelled (immediately at SendGrid for email) before eventManager.reschedule runs; if the reschedule subsequently fails, the still-active original booking is left with its reminders already cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, when originalRescheduledBooking?.uid is present, the code cancels that booking’s workflow reminders *before* calling eventManager.reschedule (new block around lines ~961+). For email it calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true), and emailReminderManager.ts shows immediateDelete=true triggers an external SendGrid cancel (POST status=cancel) and then returns without marking the DB reminder as cancelled or otherwise tying it to a successful reschedule. There is no transactional/rollback linkage to eventManager.reschedule, so if reschedule throws/fails, the original booking can remain active while its reminders have already been cancelled externally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-50 — remindersToCancel is not filtered by method: EMAIL, scheduled: true, or referenceId: null; any row lacking a valid SendGrid batch id would send batch_id: null and trigger the whole-loop abort described in issue 1.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `remindersToCancel` is fetched with only `where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` and then every result is cancelled via SendGrid using `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` inside `client.request(...)`. The diff shows no filtering by `method === EMAIL`, `scheduled === true`, or `referenceId != null`, so non-email reminders (e.g., SMS) or rows with a null/invalid `referenceId` would still be sent to the SendGrid cancel endpoint, likely erroring. Because the whole loop is wrapped in a single `try`, one failure would skip cancellation/deletion for subsequent reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:489 vs packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — The two reschedule flows use different email-cancellation semantics (deferred flag vs immediateDelete: true), so the old booking's emails are cancelled with different timing and guarantees depending on which reschedule path executes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two reschedule paths cancelling email reminders with different semantics. In `handleNewBooking.ts` (around the added block near line ~966), reschedule cancels old booking reminders via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, which triggers the `immediateDelete` branch in `emailReminderManager.ts` (POST cancel to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` and returns without marking `cancelled`). In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (around ~489), the reschedule path calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` with no third argument, which takes the non-immediate path and merely sets `WorkflowReminder.cancelled = true` in DB. This difference is real and means timing/guarantees of cancellation depend on which reschedule flow runs, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it always causes incorrect behavior (it may be intentional deferred cancellation handled later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:374-381 — The previous deleteMany enforced booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }; the reminder managers now delete by bare id with no ownership check, removing defense-in-depth against deleting other users' reminders if the upstream fetch query is ever broadened.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` the prior code deleted reminders via `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})`, which added an ownership constraint at deletion time. The diff replaces that with calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`. In the updated managers, the Prisma operations (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` in `smsReminderManager.ts` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete/update({ where: { id: reminderId }})` in `emailReminderManager.ts`) operate on bare `id` with no user/booking scoping. The current router likely only iterates reminders fetched for the current user, so this isn’t a proven exploitable security bug from the diff alone, but it is a concrete defense-in-depth regression tied to this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder no longer deletes anything in its default path (it flips a flag and depends on a cron run up to an hour before send time); the name and the 'delete' call-site comments no longer match the actual contract, which is misleading for maintainers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` was changed to, by default (`referenceId` present and `immediateDelete` not set), only `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` rather than cancelling/deleting the scheduled send or deleting the DB row (emailReminderManager.ts). Actual cancellation/deletion is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which now queries `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour and then calls the provider cancel endpoint and deletes them. Multiple call sites and comments still use “delete” wording while the default contract is now “mark cancelled for later cleanup,” which is misleading for maintainers, but not provably a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] No tests were added for the new cancellation behavior — deleteScheduledEmailReminder's three branches, deleteScheduledSMSReminder's error coupling, the cron cancel loop, and the cancel/reschedule handler changes — despite the significant behavioral shift from immediate row deletion to deferred flag-based cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new cancellation logic (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` with three distinct branches in `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now always deleting the DB row in `smsReminderManager.ts`, the new cron-like cancellation loop in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that finds `cancelled: true` reminders within 1 hour and then cancels + deletes them, and multiple call-site behavior changes in `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `handleNewBooking.ts`, and TRPC routers shifting from immediate `workflowReminder.deleteMany` to flagging `cancelled`). No test files or test updates appear in the provided diff to cover these new branches/flows, so the test-gap concern is specific and diff-grounded but not itself a functional defect.
